The refund account concerns earlier ICOs, and the webpage and company names do not establish an endorsement, guaranteed forecast, or harmful outcome.

opening.argument: Judge the forecast together with the action requested. The speaker says a coin bought for $18 will become $90 by 2027, calling that his minimum target, then advises viewers to buy seven coins if they intend to hold five. He also presents a $9,000 profit scenario. That is more than a detached discussion of price: the projected appreciation is used to make a specific token purchase and holding plan attractive. The evidence does not prove that the price will rise, which is precisely why the confident return claim matters when viewers are being urged to put money into the token.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The disclaimer does not erase the spoken purchase advice. Nor does calling the $90 figure a forecast change how it is delivered: the speaker says the coin “will become” $90 and calls it a “minimum target.” The defense points to freedom not to buy, but that addresses viewer choice, not whether a projected return is being used to solicit a purchase.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The cited return is the speaker's future price target, not evidence that the return is guaranteed or that a viewer bought anything. The purchase advice sits alongside instructions to trade some tokens and buy during a market crash, reflecting an investment opinion exposed to market movement. The description explicitly warns that every investment and trade involves risk and calls for viewers to do their own research.

opening.argument: Consider the signals in combination. The speaker recounts turning a $250 ICO investment into a $12,250 profit, claims large companies are secretly buying AVX, and then presents $18 as a low price against a former $146 high. Those claims can make an uncertain token purchase feel like a rare opportunity backed by informed buyers and a dramatic personal success story. The account supplies no basis for treating that earlier ICO outcome as evidence that AVX will follow it; its persuasive force comes from placing the windfall story beside the present buying case.

citations.quote: i had a profit of 12,250$ They wasn't even expecting and i have invested only $250
like this AVX tokens that are large companies are secretly buying them
We can buy all the money time high was $ 146. Today's price is $18 it's undervalued coin

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense is right that the refund story concerns earlier ICOs, but that does not address how the earlier profit story is used here: the speaker explicitly likens AVX to the token he says made him a good profit. Likewise, saying viewers are free not to buy does not substantiate the claim that large companies are secretly buying. These are reasons to scrutinize the pitch, even without a proven loss.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The earlier gain is expressly an account of another token, not an AVX result. The speaker's comparison and assertion about company buying do not establish that the AVX forecast is fraudulent. His description also warns against investing money one cannot afford to lose. These signals warrant skepticism about the prediction, but the cited material does not show a deceptive transaction or promised recovery of the viewer's money.

opening.argument: The news-and-analysis presentation functions as a buying pitch. After discussing network use, the speaker claims BlackRock has placed Avalanche in its portfolio and names Citibank among companies associated with it; the sampled webpage displays BlackRock and Citi beneath a headline about businesses trusting Avalanche. He then moves to a $90 price target and advice to pay for seven coins to hold five. Whatever the business relationships actually mean, presenting those names next to an explicit purchase recommendation invites viewers to treat institutional association as support for token appreciation. The webpage alone does not establish that those businesses endorse buying the token.

citations.quote: And its because BlackRock liked them so much and has given them a place in its portfolio Other than BlackRock there are many companies who have invested into it
If we buy one coin, it will become 90 dollars by 2027. This is my minimum target.
Now I will advise you if you want to hold 5 ABX tokens then pay for 7 coins

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense says the webpage and company names do not establish an endorsement. That is the concern: a page about businesses trusting a network cannot establish that those businesses recommend purchasing its coin or validate the speaker's $90 target. The defense's characterization as analysis also leaves out the direct advice to buy more coins than the proposed long-term holding.

citations.quote: If we buy one coin, it will become 90 dollars by 2027. This is my minimum target.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The webpage's business-trust message is not a token endorsement, but the opening identifies no statement on that page promising a return. The speaker offers a price prediction and trading advice; those can be promotional without establishing a scam. The description expressly frames the opinion as informational and warns that investments and trading involve risk.
